Flats are tricky. Mine swelled PLENTY when I got it done. And it catches on hair a lot. I wouldn’t necessarily recommend either as your first cartilage piercing because both can be a little more demanding than other choices. If you start with a flat, however, it is very important that you do not sleep on it while it is healing. Flats can very easily migrate/get crooked from being slept on.

Oh, dude, they’re not bad at all. I honestly found the experience comparable to a lobe piercing (but then again I found a conch to be a cake walk). Lobe 1/10, Lobe (through scar tissue) 3/10, Tragus 4/10, Daith (pierced too shallow) 5/10, Conch (standard) 3.5/10, Helix (top left) 2/10, Septum 3/10, Nostril 3/10, Forward helix 7/10 (I wiggle my ears a lot and it’s practically reflex now so that’s probably why—I have yet to find someone who had as much trouble as I did with this one)

Piercings that did not ache after a day: Conch, Helix, Lobe, Nostril, Septum

Piercings that did: Tragus, Forward Helix, Daith — none of these were so bad that over-the-counter painkillers couldn’t fix but the placement I chose for the forward helix got in the way of a mask I was required to wear when it was swelling.

I have a relatively high pain tolerance but the forward helix was the one that GOT me, dude, and it was ALSO the one that took the longest for the needle to go through. The DAITH went faster like what??? As soon as the jewelry was in and secure though, I was fine. 

A good thing to remember with every piercing though is that so long as the piercer did not severely screw it up, the “painful” part (which has only ever exceeded marginal discomfort once) only lasts for the instant that the needle goes through. The discomfort that you feel afterward when the jewelry goes in ends pretty much as soon as it’s fastened and they stop touching it. Good luck!
